name: Frozen Custard
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: powdered loaf-sugar
ingredients.originalText: half a pound of powdered loaf-sugar

instructions.text: Slice a vanilla bean and boil it slowly in half a pint of milk till all the strength is extracted and the milk highly flavoured with the vanilla.
Strain it and set it aside.
Mix a quart of cream and a pint of milk into a skillet or sauce-pan.
Set it on hot coals and boil it.
When it has come to a boil, mix a table-spoonful of flour in three table-spoonfuls of milk and stir it into the boiling liquid.
Beat six eggs with two table-spoonfuls of milk and pour them slowly into the mixture.
Stir it all the time it is boiling.
Five minutes after, stir in gradually half a pound of powdered loaf-sugar and then the decoction of vanilla.
Stir it hard a few moments and take it off the fire.
When quite cold, put it into a mould and freeze it as you would ice-cream.

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Slice a vanilla bean and boil it slowly in half a pint of milk till all the strength is extracted and the milk highly flavoured with the vanilla.
2. Strain it and set it aside.
3. Mix a quart of cream and a pint of milk into a skillet or sauce-pan.
4. Set it on hot coals and boil it.
5. When it has come to a boil, mix a table-spoonful of flour in three table-spoonfuls of milk and stir it into the boiling liquid.
6. Beat six eggs with two table-spoonfuls of milk and pour them slowly into the mixture.
7. Stir it all the time it is boiling.
8. Five minutes after, stir in gradually half a pound of powdered loaf-sugar and then the decoction of vanilla.
9. Stir it hard a few moments and take it off the fire.
10. Set it to cool.
11. When quite cold, put it into a mould and freeze it as you would ice-cream.
